nodes.label: Q2: Inside Success rollout
nodes.explain: Decision 0011 paused the Inside Success team rollout until whygame5 produced a result under AES; that condition was met on 2026-09-26 and the call to resume was never made. The one-tool design says any repository, personal or Inside Success, installs Lockstep with one command; slice 6 merged on 2026-11-12 and Team-Brains' Project Brain runner, an Inside Success repository, now vendors Lockstep's wheel (Team-Brains#1183, wiki/lockstep.md:22). Close the old rollout item, or keep it open? Recommendation: Close decision 0011 item 4: the rollout it paused was of the v0.2 `aes` command line, which now retires. Putting Lockstep into Inside Success repositories is slice 6 of the one-tool plan and would come to you then as its own decision. Default: The rollout stays paused and decision 0011 item 4 stays as written. Team-Brains' runner already vendors the wheel, so the call to keep that and to close or keep item 4 is now to be made about work that has shipped.

nodes.label: Q6: When AES's own .aes/ retires
nodes.explain: Decision 0010 accepted v0.2 with nine criteria supported; `make aes` now reports 2 of 12 supported and 52 of 55 observations stale. Code2-workspace decision 0009 (a) retires the `aes` command line and `.aes/target.yaml` in each repository when it is next changed, and the one-tool design keeps `.aes/target.yaml` readable only until lifelike and Team-Brains move off it (slice 2, merged in #835 with `.aes/target.yaml` still read, wiki/lockstep.md:30; this repository's `.aes/` folder and `make aes` are still here). Should this repository's own `.aes/` folder and `make aes` target be removed in the one-tool build, and in which slice, rather than re-recording evidence for a retiring engine? Settled by: An argument settles it: decision 0009 (a) says the folder goes when the repository is next changed, and the one-tool build changes it; Lockstep imports this repository's library (src/agentic_engineering_system), not its `.aes/` folder, so the folder and `make aes` can go in the slice that stops reading `.aes/target.yaml` (slice 2) without breaking Lockstep. Re-recording evidence for the retiring engine is not worth doing. The Lockstep session confirms the slice when it plans slice 2.
